title: Loaded crushed potatoes with spring onion beans

grandparents_cupboard.reason: Potatoes, butter, tinned beans, crème fraîche, Cheddar, pears and watercress are all ordinary home foods with nothing factory-made.

supermarket.reason: Every ingredient is an everyday item at Tesco or any mainstream supermarket.

basic_kitchen.reason: It needs only a pan, a frying pan and a grater, with simple boiling and frying.

works.reason: 800g potatoes, a tin of beans, 150g crème fraîche and 80g Cheddar with a side salad make a sensible lunch for four, and 15 minutes is right for halved small potatoes.

honest_times.reason: Fifteen minutes of halving potatoes, slicing spring onions and pears and grating cheese is believable, and the 15-minute cook matches the boil, so it suits a quick lunch.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed ingredient and seasoning is used in the steps, the names match their ids, and nothing unlisted appears apart from water.

seasonal_feel.reason: Two bunches of spring onions flavour the bean topping named in the title, and a warm potato lunch suits mid-October.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are clear, plain British English a beginner could follow.

hearty_healthy.reason: Potatoes, beans, cheese and a pear and watercress salad make a filling, balanced family lunch.
